movielens.lineup_name: One genre — a science fiction season
movielens.source: MovieLens 32M, GroupLens Research, University of Minnesota
movielens.headline: Annihilation and Stalker are the two films a genre tag would call identical, and the two Qloo puts furthest apart. The 777 people who rated both agree.
movielens.limit: Rating agreement is not festival attendance. No public dataset records which people attended which screenings, so this tests whether the taste signal tracks observed preference, not whether two films share a room.
movielens.baseline_verdict: Every film in this set carries the Sci-Fi tag, and the tag predicts nothing: +0.038 against Qloo's -0.498. Release year carries a little signal at -0.139. Popularity none. Cultural affinity is thirteen times the strongest predictor of whether two films' viewers agree.

entity_probe.verdict: Artists resolve better than films and separate more sharply, but the cutoff holds only within ±0.01 against film's ±0.05. One lineup cannot justify a cutoff that fragile, so Slate stays with one entity type.
